lesson_title: Your Class's Morning Commute, Drawn as a City
hook_text: Thirty travel times. One skyline. Suddenly the whole class's morning is visible in a single glance.
clip_script: Thirty learners wrote down their travel time to school — a useless jumble of numbers, until you sort it. Five buckets: under ten minutes, tens, twenties, thirties, forties. Count each bucket: 3, 8, 11, 5, 3. Now stand the counts up as towers, side by side, touching — because time flows, 19,9 minutes runs straight into 20. What you get is a skyline, and skylines read instantly. Downtown — the tallest tower — sits over the twenties: that is where the class crowds. The suburbs sprawl right: a thinning tail of learners crossing half the city every morning. One glance and you can say it all: a typical commute is about 24 minutes, times stretch from a five-minute walk to a fifty-minute mission, and the long tail points right. That is a histogram — thirty stories, one picture.
visual_style: Numbers raining into five glowing buckets, buckets rising into a neon city skyline along a minutes axis, a spotlight sweeping from the tallest tower out along the right-hand tail as caption sentences stamp in.
pacing: Fast sort, rhythmic tower raises on each count, a pause as the skyline completes, smooth glide through the three reading beats.
